results.evidence: Eighth pass, 2026-10-01. Live row: day 1 4.5 mi (r14), day 2 miles 7.7 with the note already restating the sourced '~4.5 miles back out'; dist_km null. Day 2 is Goat Flat -> lookout -> Goat Flat -> trailhead, so only a source stating that whole day, or the segments in words, could settle it without a sum. Found: (1) Washington Hiking / Pacific Northwest Hiking (one author, several editions; Internet Archive full-text search): from Goat Flats the trail 'continues 1 mile to Tin Can Gap and another mile to an old lookout atop Three Fingers' (about 2 mi one way). (2) A 2026 trip report from Goat Flats camp: '2.7 miles + 2150 feet' from camp to the lookout (one way), on a three-day trip whose days start at the road washout. (3) A WTA trip report summary (search extract only) has the lookout as about 3-3.5 mi beyond Goat Flats; another search extract gives 4.5 mi round trip. (4) A bike-and-hike overnight account gives only the totals (about seven miles of hiking each way, 33 mi round trip with the bike). (5) 75 Scrambles in Washington lists Tin Can Gap at 6 mi (r14) but its lookout entry was not readable (lend-only scan). Goat Flat -> lookout is therefore ~2 / 2.7 / 3-3.5 mi one way, one author each, and no source states a day-2 total; writing one would need arithmetic. The note's '~4.5 miles back out' is already the sourced segment. No ops.

results.evidence: Eighth pass, 2026-10-01. Live waypoint 5: 'Walrus (Clark) Glacier rope-up / crevasse zone' at 48.05036669713597, -120.93634128570551, elev 6700, moved there by r5 (README section 8) from 48.04725024,-120.96234512 (8,025 ft ground). The task's '7,000 vs 8,025' description is stale. What the point is: two independent accounts put the rope-up on a bench on Clark's eastern arm reached after dropping off the far side of Boulder Pass. (1) A 2013 trip report: 'headed northeasterly to 6300-foot Boulder Pass. We dropped down steep snow on the other side of the pass, then ascended to a 6700-foot bench on Clark's eastern arm. This bench provided a good place to rope up ... We wrapped around the eastern arm and got our first view of the Walrus Glacier.' (2) The Walrus Glacier route page (archived): trip stats '12:00 6100' left camp for summit; 12:40 6760' roped up; 2:30 8000' col; 3:15 8600' reached summit ... 6:30 6760' unroped'. A third (2019 report behind the GPS track used in r5): dropped ~150 ft from the pass, crossed the basin north-west, climbed ~500 ft to the top of the ridge, reached the glacier, roped up. The pin's position (published map marker '6700' + recorded track, r5) and its 6,700 elev match these; USGS reads 6,617 ft there. Text defects: (a) note 'Rope up here east of Boulder Pass' - the accounts reach the bench over the pass and across the basin to the north-west, not east of the pass, so the bearing is replaced by the named place (no computed bearing written). (b) directions said to traverse on from the bench, 'turn back west ... to the toe of the glacier', and 'Rope up here' - i.e. rope up at the toe; both accounts rope up on the bench itself (as the row's own climbing_route step 1 and itinerary day 2 already say). The traverse wording beneath Peak 7242 is kept unchanged; only where the rope goes on is corrected. Name and type are left (owner may prefer 'Rope-up bench on Clark's eastern arm'). No pin op: the coordinate is already sourced.

results.evidence: Eighth pass, 2026-10-01. Live access.permit: 'Free self-issue Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit, filled out at the trailhead; required for day use as well as overnight, no quota.'. access.fees (not touched) says 'no wilderness permit needed since this route stays outside the adjacent Alpine Lakes Wilderness', so the two fields contradict. Boundary (land manager's own data, USFS EDW wilderness layer, point queries): every pin, index 0-6 including the summit block (index 5) and the summit (index 6, 47.439074,-121.44408), returns no wilderness polygon, while a 25 m search radius around the summit returns Alpine Lakes Wilderness. So the climb is outside and the summit is within 25 m of the line. OpenStreetMap independently puts a point about 240 m north-west of the summit inside the Alpine Lakes Wilderness (the summit query itself timed out on both Overpass servers). Permit rule (land manager): MBS 'Wilderness Regulations' page: 'Day-use and overnight visitors to the Alpine Lakes Wilderness will need to fill-out a free, self-issue permit available at ranger stations and trailheads'; the Snow Lake Trail 1013 page (same trailhead lot) says permits are required for day use and overnight trips. Climbing sources list the peak under the wilderness: the club route page's land-manager field reads 'Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest Alpine Lakes Wilderness' (it says nothing about a permit), and the peak database lists the Alpine Lakes Wilderness (r1). No written source says a permit is not needed. Since the summit sits on the line and a wrong 'no permit' risks a citation while carrying a free permit costs nothing, the sentence keeps the permit and scopes the wilderness fact: outside on the way up, boundary at the summit. Row + land-manager data suffice for a permit fact; the boundary fact also has the row's own pins and access.fees. Season dates (May 15-Oct 31, one land-manager page) are not added. The overnight_permit object already names the same permit and is left. NOT touched: access.fees ('no wilderness permit needed ...') - owner, drop that clause or leave it; with this wording it no longer contradicts on where the route runs, only on whether the permit is needed. access._raw not touched.
